==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|considre||archaic}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|consideren}}, from {{der|en|frm|considerer}}, from {{der|en|la|considero|considerare}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/kənˈsɪd.ə/|a=RP,AuE}}
* {{IPA|en|/kənˈsɪd.əɹ/|[kənˈsɪɾ.ɚ]|[kn̩ˈsɪɾ.ɚ]|a=GA,CA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-consider.ogg|a=California}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkən.sɪ.ɖə(r)/|a=Indic}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪdə(ɹ)|s=3}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[think]] about [[seriously]].
#: {{syn|en|bethink|[[reflect]] ([[on]])|take|Thesaurus:ponder}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Consider''' that we’ve had three major events and the year has hardly begun.}}
#: {{ux|en|How can you know everything about everything, if you won't '''consider''' any dissent?}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=8|passage=Thenceforth to speculations high or deep / I turned my thoughts, and with capacious mind / '''Considered''' all things visible.|year=1873}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2014-03-15|volume=410|issue=8878| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21598997-american-regulators-should-block-comcasts-proposed-deal-time-warner-cable-turn-it Turn it off]| passage=If the takeover is approved, Comcast would control 20 of the top 25 cable markets, […]. Antitrust officials will need to '''consider''' Comcast’s status as a monopsony (a buyer with disproportionate power), when it comes to negotiations with programmers, whose channels it pays to carry.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To think about something seriously or carefully: to [[deliberate]].
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:ponder}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To think about whether one will do (an action); to weigh as a possible course of action. 
#: {{syn|en|think of|bethink}}
#: {{ux|en|I’m '''considering''' going to the beach tomorrow.}}
# {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To [[assign]] some [[quality]] to.
#: {{syn|en|deem|regard|think of|Thesaurus:deem}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Consider''' yourself lucky, but '''consider''' your opponent skillful.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''considered''' the pie undercooked.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''consider''' you (to be) an excellent friend.}}
#* {{RQ:Austen Pride and Prejudice|passage="What a charming amusement for young people this is, Mr. Darcy! There is nothing like dancing after all. I '''consider''' it as one of the first refinements of polished society."}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=Foreword|passage=‘I understand that the district was '''considered''' a sort of sanctuary,’ the Chief was saying. ‘An Alsatia like the ancient one behind the Strand, or the Saffron Hill before the First World War.{{nb...}}’}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Paul Glader|title=Four takeaways from Walter Isaacson’s biography of Elon Musk|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/12/tech/elon-musk-isaacson-biography-takeaways/index.html|date=2023-09-12|passage=Isaacson reports that Musk’s fractured relationship with Jenna, who is trans, partly led to Musk’s rightward turn toward libertarianism and questioning what he '''considers''' the “woke-mind-virus, which is fundamentally antiscience, antimerit, and antihuman.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260412195435/https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/12/tech/elon-musk-isaacson-biography-takeaways/index.html|archivedate=12 April 2026}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[look]] at [[attentively]].
#: {{syn|en|regard|observe|Thesaurus:pay attention}}
#: {{ux|en|She sat there for a moment, '''considering''' him.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Proverbs|31|16||She '''considereth''' a field, and buyeth it.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[take up]] as an [[example]].
#: {{syn|en|take}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Consider''' a triangle having three equal sides.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|parliamentary procedure}} To [[debate]] (or [[dispose]] of) a [[motion]].
#: {{syn|en|deliberate|bethink}}
#: {{ux|en|This body will now '''consider''' the proposed amendments to Section 453 of the zoning code.}}
# To have regard to; to take into view or account; to pay due attention to; to respect.
#: {{syn|en|take into account|hear}}
#: {{ux|en|He never seems to '''consider''' the feelings of others.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Cymbeline|act=V|scene=v|passage='''Consider''', sir, the chance of war: the day / Was yours by accident.}}
#* '''February 21, 1679''', {{w|Sir William Temple, 1st Baronet|William Temple}}, ''letter to the Lord Treasurer''
# To [[believe]] or [[opine]] (that).
#* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=2|passage=Mother very rightly resented the slightest hint of condescension. She '''considered''' that the exclusiveness of Peter's circle was due not to its distinction, but to the fact that it was an inner Babylon of prodigality and whoredom,{{...}}.}}
#* {{quote-web|en|title=''Party A v. British Columbia (Securities Commission),'' 2021 BCCA 358 |author=J. Susan Griffin|url=https://canlii.ca/t/jjchh|work=CanLII|date=1 October 2021|accessdate=3 October 2021|text=What is clear is that the courts in both Alberta and Ontario '''consider''' that there must be some preliminary assessment of the evidence of alleged breaches of the relevant Act when considering whether a freeze order is justified at the investigation stage.}}

====Usage notes====
* In sense 3, this is a [[catenative verb]] that takes the gerund ([[-ing]]). See [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]].
